pr_title: fix(discovery): make discovery manager notify consumers of dropped targets for still defined jobs
pr_body:
See https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/12858#issuecomment-1812193655 for details (will add that to the commit message)

I added a test that reproduces: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/12858#issuecomment-1732318102 and it's failing with the code in main: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/actions/runs/6876250042/job/18701456148?pr=13147#step:6:378

I pushed a draft fix (see comments in the code)

fixes https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/12858


---

**>>>>>>> NOTE:**

This fix concerns the SD manager behind the flag `new-service-discovery-manager` which is the manager used by most third parties but not the one used by default by Prometheus itself, as of now, Prometheus is still using the legacymanager  https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/d63f5b35df0f96b02961eff59205336812575689/discovery/legacymanager/manager.go#L14 by default. The plan is to switch to the new manager in 3.0 https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/13609

issue_context.title: kubernetes_sd does not remove existing targets when an existing config is modified to produce an empty result
issue_context.body:
Maybe related to https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/10257

### What did you do?

1. Create a Prometheus configuration with a kubernetes_sd_configs that has a non-empty target discovery.
2. Start Prometheus with this configuration.
3. Verify that Prometheus is scraping the targets that are discovered by the kubernetes_sd_configs.
4. Modify the kubernetes_sd_configs to produce an empty result.
5. Reload the Prometheus configuration.


### What did you expect to see?

When the kubernetes_sd_configs is modified to produce an empty result, Prometheus should remove all of the targets that were discovered by the kubernetes_sd_configs before it was modified.

When an existing  kubernetes_sd_configs is modified so that the targets discovered change without producing an empty result the targets in prometheus update correctly on reload, in both cases where more or less targets are discovered.

### What did you see instead? Under which circumstances?

The discovered targets are still present and being scraped until prometheus is restarted

Maybe related: I have observed that if you (re)start Prometheus with a kubernetes_sd_configs that produces an empty result, nothing shows on the URLs /targets or /service-discovery related to this config.

### System information

Linux 6.4.15-200.fc38.x86_64  (also seen on different setups local and k8s) 

### Prometheus version

```text
prometheus --version

  go version:       go1.21.0
  platform:         linux/amd64
  tags:             netgo,builtinassets,stringlabels
```
Also seen on prometheus 2.45.0

### Prometheus configuration file


comments:
I've been able to reproduce this with much simpler config, both with `kubernetes_sd_config` and `file_sd_config`. For instance, if one starts with the following:

```yaml
---
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: test
    kubernetes_sd_configs:
      - role: pod
        kubeconfig_file: somekubeconfig
```

All pods in the cluster will be discovered. When changing that to the following though, adding a namespace that contains no pods or does not exist:

```yaml
---
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: test
    kubernetes_sd_configs:
      - role: pod
        kubeconfig_file: somekubeconfig
        namespaces:
          names:
            - default
```

All previously discovered pods will remain. But it's not limited to Kubernetes SD:

```yaml
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: testFile
    file_sd_configs:
      - files:
        - foo.yml
```

If `foo.yml` contains some hosts, and is then emptied, or the path changed to a file that does not exist, those targets will also still remain.

I did some digging for the `file_sd_configs` case (replacing an existing file with a non existing one) and I think I understand where the leak happens.

**(I'm talking about `new-service-discovery-manager` in here)**

During the reload, the discovery manager will get rid of the obsolete provider/discoverer that used to take care of the initial file (discover the targets in it etc.):

https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/cf528bef034dcf078d3bff0d50224a13068c391e/discovery/manager.go#L211-L219

this will run the provider's "cleanup code":

https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/cf528bef034dcf078d3bff0d50224a13068c391e/discovery/manager.go#L297-L303

The problem is that it drops the discovered targets from `m.targets` and never tells the concerned consumers (scrapers e.g.) to forget about them, next updates would never deal with them:

https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/cf528bef034dcf078d3bff0d50224a13068c391e/discovery/manager.go#L354

https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/cf528bef034dcf078d3bff0d50224a13068c391e/discovery/manager.go#L393-L410

And because the `job` is still defined in the config file, the consumers (scrape manager e.g.) will keep the entry for it with the expired targets.

I have a test that reproduces this and a drat fix for this.


For the "empty the file" case, the `file` discoverer already takes care of expiring the targets (I tested with `new-service-discovery-manager`), maybe we should add a unit test for this if it's missing 

I think this leak concerns all the service discoverers that send partial states/updates (files, kubernetes, zk etc.):

https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/cf528bef034dcf078d3bff0d50224a13068c391e/discovery/manager.go#L154-L156

I'll re-open this as the attached fix only addresses the SD manager behind the `new-service-discovery-manager` flag.
Personally, I do not plan to debug and fix this for the legacy/default DS manager, but I'm happy to assist if anyone else is interested in taking it on.
The plan is to make `new-service-discovery-manager` the default for Prometheus 3. https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/13609
Hello from the bug scrub! The new SD manager is now the default and should have fixed this according to the comment, thus we're closing this issue as completed.
